positive_change.result: La publication du livre "On the Origin of Species" par Charles Darwin a permis de comprendre scientifiquement l'évolution des espèces par sélection naturelle.
positive_change.beneficiaries: Les scientifiques, élèves, et tous ceux qui s'intéressent à la diversité du vivant dans le monde entier.

fact_checks.sentence: En 1859, Charles Darwin a publié "On the Origin of Species", apportant une explication scientifique à l'évolution des populations par sélection naturelle.
source_passages: Home This Day In History Good News in History, November 24 167 years ago today, the British naturalist and geologist Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species explaining his theory of evolution.

fact_checks.sentence: Ce livre, considéré comme l'un des plus influents, a fondé la théorie selon laquelle la diversité des espèces résulte d'une ascendance commune et de processus évolutifs sur plusieurs générations.
source_passages: The first edition—which has been voted by publishers and librarians as the most influential academic book ever written—introduced the scientific theory that populations evolve over the course of generations through a process of natural selection.
It presented a body of evidence that the diversity of life arose by common descent through a tree-like branching pattern of evolution.

fact_checks.sentence: L'ouvrage présente des preuves issues d'expéditions et d'expériences, validant la sélection naturelle comme mécanisme testable.
source_passages: WATCH an animation about how little finches were crucial to his discovery, and how pepper moths evolved due to pollution… (1859) Darwin included evidence that he had gathered on expeditions to South America in the 1830s and his subsequent findings from research and experimentation, and showed how natural selection is a scientifically testable mechanism.

fact_checks.sentence: Aujourd'hui, cette théorie demeure un pilier central des sciences de la vie, soutenue par des analyses génomiques modernes.
source_passages: Modern evolutionary theory continues to develop, but his writings still explain the diversity of living organisms and their adaptation to the environment; make sense of the geological record; and hold up under modern genome analysis.

fact_checks.sentence: Ainsi, Darwin a modifié durablement la manière dont la biodiversité et l'adaptation au milieu sont comprises à l'échelle mondiale.
source_passages: Within two decades widespread scientific agreement solidified that evolution had occurred, and by the mid-20th century Darwin’s concept of evolutionary adaptation through natural selection became central to modern evolutionary theory—and the unifying concept of the life sciences.

positive_change.result: Les îles-barrières près de Point Lay en Alaska ont été officiellement protégées, assurant un refuge permanent pour environ 200 000 morses du Pacifique et conservant un des plus vastes systèmes de lagunes côtières intactes au monde.
positive_change.beneficiaries: Les morses du Pacifique, en particulier les femelles et les jeunes, qui utilisent ces îles pour se reposer et échapper à la perte de la glace de mer ; ainsi que les communautés tribales locales qui pratiquent la chasse traditionnelle.

fact_checks.sentence: Dans la région de Point Lay sur la côte de la mer de Béring, une zone de 47 000 acres a été consacrée à la protection des îles-barrières qui accueillent désormais la plus importante concentration de morses du Pacifique en Amérique du Nord.
source_passages: Home to the largest concentrations of Pacific walrus found anywhere in North America, the barrier islands off the coast of the tiny northern village of Point Lay provide a critical refuge for these marine megafauna.

Now ensconced within a 47,000-acre protected area (74 square miles) held by the Interior Alaska Land Trust, the islands have been spared from industrial development and other disturbances, as has “one of the largest, undiminished coastal lagoon systems in the world,” which was protected in tandem.

fact_checks.sentence: Ce site, essentiel depuis 2007 lorsque les morses ont changé leur comportement de migration en raison de la fonte de la glace arctique, offre un espace de repos sûr, notamment aux femelles et aux jeunes.
source_passages: Part of the coalition that for 10 years has worked towards securing protections for the Point Lay barrier islands and the Kasegaluk Lagoon, The Conservation Fund explains that the islands hadn’t historically been a walrus mecca until 2007, when the animals changed their seasonal migration behavior in mass.
Historically, these animals relied on Arctic sea ice for resting spots, but by 2007 the ice had become inconsistent.
One year, an estimated 200,000 walrus hauled themselves up onto the barrier islands of Point Lay, and they’ve returned every year ever since.

That includes every single female and juvenile Pacific walrus on Earth—all stuffed onto beaches that will now forever be theirs thanks to The Conservation Fund and its partners among the Alaska tribal nations and the Interior Alaska Land Trust.

fact_checks.sentence: Le Conservation Fund, en coopération avec les nations tribales et le Interior Alaska Land Trust, a établi une servitude de conservation qui interdit les développements industriels et limite les perturbations humaines croissantes.
source_passages: Now ensconced within a 47,000-acre protected area (74 square miles) held by the Interior Alaska Land Trust, the islands have been spared from industrial development and other disturbances, as has “one of the largest, undiminished coastal lagoon systems in the world,” which was protected in tandem.

That includes every single female and juvenile Pacific walrus on Earth—all stuffed onto beaches that will now forever be theirs thanks to The Conservation Fund and its partners among the Alaska tribal nations and the Interior Alaska Land Trust.

The new conservation easement, held by the Trust, will increase monitoring and stewardship to actively minimize disturbance to walrus and other animals as commercial and tourist activity in the Alaskan Arctic continues to expand.

fact_checks.sentence: Le travail de John Lasseter, réalisateur de films d’animation, inaugure quant à lui l’usage de l’image numérique dans la culture populaire contemporaine.
source_passages: Home This Day In History Good News in History, November 22 31 years ago today, Toy Story, the world’s first computer-animated film was released to critical acclaim.

Made out of a small studio called Pixar which released some of the most beloved children’s films in American history, the story revolves around the life and times of a boy’s favorite cowboy action figure named Woody, who’s position at the top of the toy hierarchy is disrupted by the arrival of the Space Ranger Buzz Lightyear.
Grossing over $373 million worldwide, the critically acclaimed Toy Story holds a rare 100% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

With the wit and thematic sophistication of its screenplay (by Joel Cohen, Lasseter, Joss Whedon, and others) it earned an Academy Award nomination—the first-ever animated film to be honored in a writing category.

positive_change.result: Les chercheurs étudient précisément le comportement et les préférences des poissons-lions dans l'Atlantique pour mieux localiser ces espèces envahissantes.
positive_change.beneficiaries: Les écosystèmes marins de l'Atlantique et les professionnels de la pêche pouvant ainsi mieux gérer l'impact des poissons-lions.

fact_checks.sentence: Les poissons-lions, originaires de l'Indo-Pacifique, se sont établis depuis plusieurs décennies sur les côtes atlantiques américaines et des Caraïbes.
source_passages: Lionfish are native to the Indo-Pacific, but are now established along the southeast coast of the U.S., the Caribbean, and in parts of the Gulf of America.

fact_checks.sentence: En raison de l'absence de prédateurs naturels, ces poissons carnivores exercent une pression importante sur les écosystèmes locaux, consommant notamment des jeunes de poissons commerciaux comme le mérou ou le vivaneau.
source_passages: Since lionfish are not native to Atlantic waters, they have very few predators.
They are carnivores that feed on small crustaceans and fish, including the young of important commercial fish species such as snapper and grouper.

fact_checks.sentence: Les experts étudient activement les habitudes alimentaires et les préférences d'habitat du poisson-lion dans ces eaux non natives.
source_passages: Scientists are also actively studying these fish to better understand the potential threat that lionfish pose to key reef and commercial fish species.
Learning more about the habits and preferences of lionfish in non-native waters also helps experts determine where to look for these invasive fish.

fact_checks.sentence: Cette compréhension fine permet de mieux cibler les zones où ils se rassemblent et ainsi d'améliorer la gestion de cette espèce envahissante.
source_passages: Learning more about the habits and preferences of lionfish in non-native waters also helps experts determine where to look for these invasive fish.

fact_checks.sentence: Même si l'éradication totale demeure difficile, ces connaissances facilitent les interventions sur le terrain pour limiter leurs effets négatifs.
source_passages: Unfortunately, NOAA researchers have concluded that invasive lionfish populations will continue to grow and cannot be eliminated using conventional methods.
Marine invaders are nearly impossible to eradicate once established.
